stories.title: Spider-Man Could See the Cure. He Couldn’t Reach It.

sources.title: Marvel’s most impactful Spider-Man stories
sources.excerpt: The stolen ISO-36 serum could save May. Machinery traps Peter in a flooding room. His determination lets him escape.

sources.title: Marvel’s greatest Spider-Man moments
sources.excerpt: The article identifies issue #33, his struggle beneath industrial rubble and the importance of Aunt May and Uncle Ben to his resolve.

sources.title: Marvel’s Doctor Octopus history
sources.excerpt: Octavius’s forces hijack the substance. Spider-Man reaches the underwater hideout, recovers the serum and saves May with Dr Connors’s help.

sources.title: Marvel issue catalog and cover
sources.excerpt: The Amazing Spider-Man (1963) #33, The Final Chapter, concludes the If This Be My Destiny arc.

claims.text: Doc Ock’s forces stole the serum May needed. Peter followed to an underwater hideout.
Peter was pinned beneath heavy machinery in a flooding room, close to the serum.
Remembering Aunt May and Uncle Ben, Peter persisted and lifted the machinery.
Peter recovered the serum and saved Aunt May with Dr Connors’s assistance.
May became ill because Peter’s radioactive blood was used in a transfusion. The experimental ISO-36 was needed to save her.
The focal story appears in The Amazing Spider-Man #33, published in 1966; the larger arc spans #31–33.

stories.title: Vision Beat Himself With a Question

sources.title: Head writer Jac Schaeffer on the finale
sources.excerpt: Schaeffer explains why identical Synthezoids needed a logical resolution and distinguishes the restored data from Wanda’s emotional goodbye.

sources.title: GamesRadar / Newsarama on the two Visions
sources.excerpt: The rebuilt original and Wanda’s recreation discuss the Ship of Theseus. The conversation leads to restored memories and White Vision leaving.

sources.title: Marvel on Vision’s goodbye
sources.excerpt: Wanda cannot maintain her fictional world. Her Vision is a memory made real.

sources.title: Third-party episode transcript, identity exchange
sources.excerpt: The exchange names White Vision’s target, compares the replaced ship and a second vessel from the old wood, and distinguishes original material from blocked memory data.

claims.text: SWORD rebuilt the original body as White Vision. He fought Wanda’s magically created Vision.
Wanda’s Vision was a magical creation rather than the original physical body.
The fight becomes an identity argument using the Ship of Theseus thought experiment.
Wanda’s Vision unlocks White Vision’s blocked memories. White Vision identifies himself as Vision and flies away.
White Vision’s directive is to destroy Vision. Wanda’s Vision disputes being the true original, prompting the identity discussion.
The analogy compares a ship with replaced planks and a second ship made from restored old planks. It is then applied to their bodies and memories.
White Vision’s memory data was kept from him, not fully erased. He permits access before recognizing himself.
Restoring White Vision’s data does not make him the emotional partner Wanda knew inside the Hex. Her goodbye to that Vision is a real goodbye.

stories.title: The Alien Who Took Thor's Hammer

sources.title: Marvel · Walt Simonson’s Thor reading guide
sources.excerpt: Issues 337–339 introduce Bill wielding Thor’s hammer and becoming an ally.

sources.title: Modern Masters · Walt Simonson interview, pages 47–48
sources.excerpt: Simonson designed Bill to look monstrous, describes the fiery unarmed duel and explains Bill needed the power to defend his people.

sources.title: Marvel Snap · Beta Ray Bill character spotlight
sources.excerpt: The spacecraft mistook Thor for a threat. Bill fought him, picked up the hammer, and was granted Thor’s power.

sources.title: Clixnexus · Beta Ray Bill origin and duel
sources.excerpt: Bill guards a refugee fleet, wins the duel in Skartheim, and rescues Thor from the lava.

sources.title: Marvel · Thor’s Mightiest Weapons
sources.excerpt: Bill wields the original hammer and bests Thor in unarmed combat. Odin arranges a weapon of Bill’s own, Stormbreaker.

claims.text: Bill fought Thor after his ship identified Thor as a threat, then wielded Thor’s hammer.
Beta Ray Bill was the champion protecting a fleet of Korbinite refugees.
The hammer deemed Bill worthy and gave him the power of Thor.
Odin set Thor and Bill a duel without hammers in a fiery world.
Bill won the duel and saved Thor from falling into lava.
Bill sought power he could use to protect his people.
Thor kept Mjolnir and Odin commissioned Stormbreaker for Beta Ray Bill.

stories.title: Doctor Doom Offered Mephisto a Trade
stories.issues: Doctor Strange and Doctor Doom: Triumph and Torment (1989)

sources.title: Marvel’s Doctor Strange story guide
sources.excerpt: Strange owed Doom a favor after becoming Sorcerer Supreme. They entered Mephisto’s realm to free Doom’s mother. Strange’s apparent betrayal was part of a larger plan.

sources.title: Marvel’s Cynthia von Doom entry
sources.excerpt: Cynthia made a pact for power and Mephisto took her soul. Doom and Strange freed it and she reached a better afterlife.

sources.title: William & Mary Comics Studies Club recap
sources.excerpt: Doom offers Strange in exchange for Cynthia. Cynthia refuses freedom at the cost of betrayal. A device Doom planted helps Strange escape.

sources.title: Slashfilm’s reading guide, with panel from the graphic novel
sources.excerpt: Cynthia rejects Doom’s bargain and disavows him. Doom had given Strange a way to free himself.

claims.text: Cynthia made a pact with Mephisto. He took her soul.
Strange owed Doom a favor after becoming Sorcerer Supreme and helped him enter Mephisto’s realm.
Doom offered Strange to Mephisto in exchange for Cynthia’s soul.
Cynthia rejected the exchange and disavowed her son.
Doom had planted a device that helped Strange break free.
Cynthia’s refusal redeemed her soul. Doom and Strange’s battle with Mephisto ended with her release to a better afterlife.

stories.title: Hellboy Rejects His Apocalyptic Destiny
stories.issues: Wake the Devil #5, with classic Hellboy premise context

sources.title: Dark Horse’s official Hellboy timeline
sources.excerpt: The timeline identifies the 1944 summoning, Professor Bruttenholm as his adoptive father, and the 1997 Hecate encounter in Wake the Devil.

sources.title: Official licensed Hellboy RPG sample
sources.excerpt: The character introduction describes a demon investigator who rejects his apocalyptic destiny. The Right Hand of Doom can release the Ogdru Jahad.

sources.title: Horn-breaking discussion identifying Wake the Devil #5
sources.excerpt: The answer identifies Wake the Devil part five, where Hecate invokes his destiny, his horns grow, and he breaks them in rejection. Movie filing scenes are distinguished from this event.

claims.text: Hellboy is a demon and paranormal investigator who refuses an apocalyptic destiny.
An occult ritual brought Hellboy to Earth as a child. Professor Bruttenholm, known as Broom, became his adoptive father.
His stone right hand is the key that can release the Ogdru Jahad and bring destruction.
In Wake the Devil #5, Hecate invokes his apocalyptic destiny. His horns grow and he breaks them off to reject it.

stories.title: Doom, Battleworld and the source of his power

sources.title: The Official Marvel Guide to Every Secret Wars
sources.excerpt: Paraphrased evidence: The 2015 story differs from 1984. Doom obtained Beyonder power, imposed worship on Battleworld, and concealed the former reality. Reed later drew an admission of inferiority from Doom; Molecule Man shifted the power to Reed.

sources.title: Secret Wars TPB: 2015 core collection
sources.excerpt: Paraphrased evidence: Collapsed realities leave a composite planet, Battleworld, whose surviving population answers to Doom. The listing collects the core 2015 event through issue9.

sources.title: Miles Morales: official in-comics history
sources.excerpt: Paraphrased evidence: Miles survives, finds hidden Molecule Man, feeds him, and later receives a restored home and mother. The returning survivors remember their earlier reality, unlike the inhabitants whose remembered world centers on Doom.

sources.title: The Future Foundation: official reading guide
sources.excerpt: Paraphrased evidence: The Foundation built a survival craft before the final catastrophe. The issue9 section describes Reed, Franklin and Molecule Man restoring the Foundation and creating worlds, with the family helping reconstruct the multiverse.

sources.title: Meet the Maker: official explainer
sources.excerpt: Paraphrased evidence: In the 2015 event, Molecule Man supplies Doom with his extraordinary power.

sources.title: Secret Wars: official nine-issue reading list
sources.excerpt: Paraphrased evidence: The opening involves a collision of the main and Ultimate universes. The event lists issues1-9 by Jonathan Hickman and Esad Ribic.

claims.text: The main and Ultimate universes collide during the final incursion.
Doom preserves pieces of destroyed realities as Battleworld and rules its survivors.
Reed and the Future Foundation prepare a life raft to survive the catastrophe.
Doom imposes worship and suppresses memory of the earlier reality.
Molecule Man is the underlying source sustaining Doom’s cosmic power.
Miles escapes the collapsing realities in a life raft.
Survivors find Molecule Man beneath Doomstadt while investigating Doom’s power.
Miles gives the hungry Molecule Man a hamburger and earns his gratitude.
Reed confronts Doom and gets him to concede Reed could have saved reality better.
Molecule Man transfers the cosmic power from Doom to Reed.
Reed’s family and the Future Foundation help rebuild realities using Franklin and Molecule Man’s powers.
Molecule Man rewards Miles with a place in the reconstructed reality and the return of his mother.
Some life-raft survivors, including Miles, remember the earlier reality.
